body:
Plan, rules and numbers: wf-context/docs-gaps/pass2.md (read "How a section is bound" first). Worktree wf-docs2, branch docs/pass2; DOCS_COMMON.md applies. Per-section list: wf-context/docs-gaps/pass2/out-before/binding-sections.md.

Rules in short: bind claims, not mentions. For each target section, cite the code its claims depend on: `pass2/dsdef.sh <file>#<Symbol> [stable|api]` prints the id (idempotent, writes `//ds:def` in this repo's style), then link the name in the sentence: [`Name`](ds:block?id=<id>). Defaults and limits cite their const. Pitfalls that state library or driver behaviour cite the code (or the test) that makes it true. Snippet-synced Go blocks stay with `task docs:snippets`; bind the prose around them. Only `//ds:def` lines may change in library files. Never run `ds scan`, `ds ack` or `ds refresh` (the coordinator scans and commits `.ds/` once at the end); `ds check` must stay at 0 errors.

Owns: `docs/drivers/`, `docs/operations/`, `docs/start/`; examples: backend-cutover, enqueue-only, graceful-drain, graceful-drain-report, hatchet-manage, hatchet-pause, hatchet-schedules, hatchet-worker, hybrid-placement, insert-contract, memory-options, migrations-export, namespaces, node-health, postgres-cluster, quickstart, redis-parity, redis-worker, regional-routing, retention, rolling-deploy, sleep-wake, sql-archive, sql-leader-election, sql-options, sql-queue-workers, sqlite-worker, start-gate, worker-balancing, worker-recycling, worker-wakeup.

Binding now: 22 pages, 183 sections describe library code (Try it and Related excluded), 6 bound.

## Bind (one line per page: target sections, bound now, the unbound ones)

- [ ] `docs/drivers/hatchet.md` (22 target, 2 bound): (top); Create the client; Configuration; What it can do and what it refuses; Queues, run management and drain; Step 1: serve queues with their own workers; Step 2: list runs; Step 3: retry a failed run; Step 4: list schedules; Step 5: drain before a deploy; Step 6: pause a workflow or a schedule; Step 7: run a schedule now, read its last fire, enqueue from web nodes; Step 8: cancel a delayed start; What Hatchet cannot do here; Pitfalls; Tenants, results and reschedule; Limitations; Known engine quirks; Reach the Hatchet SDK; Pitfalls
- [ ] `docs/drivers/hybrid.md` (7 target, 0 bound): (top); Before you start; Split schedules from runs; What it can do; Several nodes; Record run history; Pitfalls
- [ ] `docs/drivers/memory.md` (11 target, 1 bound): (top); Create the client; Set the pool, the clock, the logger and the middleware; Serve only some queues; Keep fewer or more finished runs; Stop when the work is done; Run thousands of schedules from one timer; Options; What it can do; Pitfalls
- [ ] `docs/drivers/redis.md` (16 target, 2 bound): Create the client; Set up a worker; What it can do and what it refuses; Use the features the SQL driver has; Step 1: observe run ends and ticks; Step 2: wait for a signal; Step 4: give a queue its own worker, and pause a workflow; Step 5: chain jobs and add a schedule condition; How work moves; Schedules; Shared stores; Options; Upgrading from an earlier version; Pitfalls
- [ ] `docs/drivers/sqlstore-insert-contract.md` (11 target, 0 bound): Before you start; The rows to write; Idempotency keys; Wake the workers; Step 1: start a worker that registers the workflow; Step 2: keep the statements; Step 3: describe a run and write its rows in one transaction; Step 4: insert a run due now and a delayed one; Step 5: handle a held idempotency key; What never to write; Pitfalls
- [ ] `docs/drivers/sqlstore.md` (21 target, 1 bound): (top); Before you start; Create the client; Pick a database; Workers and polling; Wake workers at once; Leases and crashed workers; Clocks, skew and one fire node; Use the database's clock; Elect one fire node; Rows per dispatcher query; Keep the hot tables small; Per-run facts, journal and bucket state; Fair turns between keys; Enqueue inside a pgx transaction; Database errors; Run IDs; Queues, pauses and run admin; Options; Pitfalls
- [ ] `docs/operations/balancing.md` (7 target, 0 bound): Before you start; Step 1: give the client a pool and queues; Step 2: pick a strategy; Step 3: set bounds and a step size; Step 4: run the balance loop; Your own strategy; Pitfalls
- [ ] `docs/operations/cutover.md` (8 target, 0 bound): (top); Before you start; Join the two backends; New work and old refs; Move the schedules; Retire the old backend; Capabilities; Pitfalls
- [ ] `docs/operations/deploy.md` (6 target, 0 bound): Run several workers; Web nodes that only enqueue; Deploy a new version while old workers run; Shut down cleanly; Give running steps a grace period, and see what was cut off; Pitfalls
- [ ] `docs/operations/migrations.md` (8 target, 0 bound): (top); Before you start; Run the migrations; Each store's migration list; Rolling back the code; Ship the SQL through your own tool; Table names and schemas; Pitfalls
- [ ] `docs/operations/namespaces.md` (5 target, 0 bound): One namespace per client; Step 1 — Give each SQL namespace a table prefix; Step 2 — Check that the namespaces do not meet; Step 3 — Do the same on Redis; Pitfalls
- [ ] `docs/operations/nodes.md` (7 target, 0 bound): Before you start; Name the node; See which node ran each attempt; List the online nodes; Health and readiness probes; Scheduler-only and worker-only processes; Pitfalls
- [ ] `docs/operations/recycling.md` (6 target, 0 bound): Before you start; Step 1: set the limits; Step 2: serve until the worker stops; Step 3: exit so the supervisor restarts you; What a recycle does; Pitfalls
- [ ] `docs/operations/regional-routing.md` (9 target, 0 bound): (top); Route each job to its region; Refuse an unknown region; Write your own router; Signals; Schedules; Manage runs across regions; Capabilities; Pitfalls
- [ ] `docs/operations/retention.md` (6 target, 0 bound): (top); Before you start; Keep finished runs for a while; Prune on your own schedule; Archive before deleting; Pitfalls
- [ ] `docs/operations/sleep-and-wake.md` (5 target, 0 bound): (top); Before you start; Wrap the clock; Schedule as usual; Pitfalls
- [ ] `docs/operations/start-gate.md` (7 target, 0 bound): (top); Before you start; Step 1 — Hold Start until the clock is synchronised; Step 2 — Expect ErrNotStarted until the gate opens; Step 3 — Ask anything else with a ReadyFunc; Step 4 — Give the wait a deadline; Pitfalls
- [ ] `docs/operations/tuning.md` (3 target, 0 bound): Housekeeping; Hatchet tunings; Pitfalls
- [ ] `docs/start/first-workflow.md` (6 target, 0 bound): (top); Before you start; Step 2 — Write the workflow; Step 3 — Register, observe run ends, start; Step 4 — Enqueue and read the status; Pitfalls
- [ ] `docs/start/install.md` (4 target, 0 bound): Step 1 — Add the core module; Step 2 — Check the install with a program; Pick your modules; Pitfalls
- [ ] `docs/start/production.md` (4 target, 0 bound): Before you start; Checklist; Items 1, 2, 7 and 15 in code; Pitfalls
- [ ] `docs/start/quickstart.md` (4 target, 0 bound): Register a workflow; Start and enqueue; Run it on SQLite; Pitfalls

## Gaps to close

- [ ] drivers/sqlstore.md, Options: `WithClock`, `WithLogger`, `WithMiddleware`, `WithJitterSource` and `DB` are only named; add a region to examples/sql-options that uses them and sync it into a step.
- [ ] Keyed delayed starts on Hatchet (`Job.RunAt` with `Job.IdempotencyKey`, a delayed `Spawn`: the `__wf_delayed` variant and its start gate) and the Hatchet Limitations table have no example: add a region to examples/hatchet-schedules (live part skips without the Hatchet env vars) and cite each Limitations row's claim to the driver code that refuses or bends.
- [ ] Def each driver's capability list first (memory, sqlstore, redis, hatchet, hybrid, regional, failover, cutover) with `dsdef.sh <file>#<Symbol> stable`, so every batch's 'which drivers' sentence can cite it; write the ids into pass2.md under 'Shared defs'.
- [ ] Cite instead of typing: `hatchet.DefaultBatchCoordinatorTimeout`, `DefaultIdempotencyMaxHold`, `DefaultVisibilityLag`; `sqlstore.LeaderOption`, `outbox.RelayOption`, `outbox.DeadFunc`, `pgxtx.Querier` are never named.

## Done when

- [ ] `python3 tools/binding.py` + `tools/batches.py` (see pass2.md) show every target section of this batch bound, or the report names the section and why it states no claim worth binding.
- [ ] `ds check` 0 errors; `task docs:wrap docs:links docs:snippets docs:words` pass; `go test -race` of every example touched.
- [ ] Report wf-context/reports/docs-p2-w3.md with before/after binding counts, defs added (id, file), Shared-file lines, Library bugs, DONE.

checklist.text: Gap: sqlstore other options (WithClock, WithLogger, WithMiddleware, WithJitterSource, DB) in examples/sql-options + step
Gap: Hatchet keyed delayed start region in examples/hatchet-schedules; Limitations rows cited
Gap: driver capability defs, ids in pass2.md Shared defs
Gap: cite hatchet Default* consts, sqlstore.LeaderOption, outbox.RelayOption, outbox.DeadFunc, pgxtx.Querier
Done: binding.py shows batch bound; ds check 0 errors; docs:wrap links snippets words pass; example tests

title: Docs pass 2: drivers, operations, start: bind to code and close gaps
